title: Effects of semaglutide on chronic kidney disease in patients with type 2 diabetes
authors: Perkovic V, Tuttle KR, Rossing P, Mahaffey KW, Mann JFE, Bakris G, et al.
followUp: median 3.4 years; stopped early after a prespecified interim analysis
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease: eGFR 50 to 75 mL/min/1.73 m2 with urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio above 300 and below 5000 mg/g, or eGFR 25 to below 50 with ratio above 100 and below 5000
funder: Supported by Novo Nordisk. The methods section describing the sponsor's role is behind the publisher's access wall in the archived copy and was not read.
result: The composite of kidney failure, at least 50% reduction in eGFR, or death from kidney-related or cardiovascular causes occurred in 331 of 1767 on semaglutide 1.0 mg weekly against 410 of 1766 on placebo (hazard ratio 0.76, 95% CI 0.66 to 0.88), 18.7% against 23.2%, an absolute difference of 4.5 percentage points over a median 3.4 years. Kidney-specific components 0.79 (0.66 to 0.94); cardiovascular death 0.71 (0.56 to 0.89); major cardiovascular events 0.82 (0.68 to 0.98); death from any cause 0.80 (0.67 to 0.95). The mean annual eGFR decline was 1.16 mL/min/1.73 m2 less steep. Serious adverse events 49.6% against 53.8%.
